Texas teacher says no homework for second-graders: Exception or trend?

I like this teacher. In a nation where even second graders can be obese, we need to let kids be kids and play outside. If teaching to the test simply must be done, let's reserve it for high-schoolers to ensure we graduate functionally literate adults.

But how are high schoolers going to have the skills to study/do homework if they don't do it in grade school?

You can't simply wave a magic wand and have kids learn the diligence required to study.

I'm a case in point - breezed through high school and first two years of college without studying or doing (much) homework. Third year I almost flunked out 'cause shit finally got real (for me). By the time I figured out that I needed to study, I had dug myself in deep.

Also, I'm all for having kids play outside, but most kids nowadays would rather play video games.

Although I still remember how annoying homework was back in my school days, I do think it's a necessity - learning, especially in abstract science fields like math, is first and foremost an act of repeating the same process over and over. It's just like training a muscle - if you don't do it frequently enough, you will not make any progress.

Homework is also important in that forces the kid to apply the gathered knowledge without the constant supervision of a teacher, even though it naturally may be argued that parents take this role instead more than often.
Wide, general rule for all second-graders? I think a good number of them could benefit from extra focus on education.
